rationale: Internally consistent and economically coherent, but it is a mechanical splice of two already-tested archive signals — the identical kinked structure of "Kinked financing slope by cash quality" with the lt/at short-leg weight lifted verbatim from "Asymmetric conjunction" — so it is closer to a cosmetic recombination than to a new mechanism, and the two components' near-collinear rankings make large incremental information unlikely.

The state-versus-change substitution is a genuine economic distinction with a credible diagnosis (the level-ROA weight loads on RMW and plausibly caps FF5 alpha), the expression matches the hypothesis and the sign is correct on both legs, though ΔROA is noisy and the winsorized-then-ranked one-year difference may dilute rather than sharpen the credibility weight.

The horizon extension is a legitimate and cleanly controlled test against Signal 1, but the cumulative five-year net external financing base is essentially the published Bradshaw–Richardson–Sloan external financing anomaly, so the marginal contribution rests entirely on the kink-plus-quality overlay, and TS_SUM over five annual observations will materially reduce coverage from the already-thin ~0.08.

The expression is internally consistent (cuts by cash-rich firms map to the most negative values, non-payers to exactly zero, matching the stated signaling logic) and the diagnosis of the failed level-based dividend signal is correct, but dividend-change signaling is a heavily studied effect and the enormous exact-zero mass will dominate the middle of the sort, making decile composition and hence ls_talpha unstable.

This is dominated by GROWTH(at,1) and is therefore largely a rediscovery of the asset-growth anomaly with a modest ROE-minus-payout tilt; additionally, RATIO(SUB(ib,dvt), ceq) is unstable or sign-flipped for firms with small or negative book equity, and winsorizing only the final difference does not repair that.

The refinancing-intensity channel (dltr scaled by the debt stock crossed with short-term cash coverage) is genuinely distinct from the net-issuance and asset-growth mechanisms already in the archive and the sign orientation is correct, but the double-rank product informs only the bad tail — the long leg pools everything with either low rollover or high coverage — so expect a one-sided spread and check whether dltr is merely proxying for short debt maturity.
